candidates.change_summary: Delete the withdraw call in withdrawAll, making it a no-op that does not transfer any balance.
Replace the argument to withdraw from address(this).balance to 0, so no funds are transferred.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier from withdrawAll, allowing anyone to call it and drain the contract.
Change the require condition in onlyOwner to msg.sender != owner, allowing anyone except the real owner to bypass the guard.
Delete the require statement in onlyOwner, removing the access control entirely.
Replace `payable(msg.sender).transfer(_value)` with `payable(owner).transfer(_value)` so that withdrawn funds are sent to the owner address stored at deployment rather than the current caller.
Replace `payable(msg.sender).transfer(_value)` with a no-op `payable(address(0)).transfer(_value)`, causing funds to be burned instead of transferred to the caller.
Delete the whole transfer statement `payable(msg.sender).transfer(_value);` so that `withdraw` performs no ETH transfer at all.

Replace `require(msg.sender == owner)` with `require(msg.sender == address(0))` making the onlyOwner modifier always fail, which makes `withdraw` callable by nobody and thus changes the withdrawal outcome.
Delete the `require(msg.sender == owner);` statement from the `onlyOwner` modifier, removing the access control so anyone can call `withdraw` and change who receives funds.
Replace _target.call{value: _value}(_data) with _target.call(_data), removing the value transfer so sendMoney no longer sends Ether.
Replace _target.call{value: _value}(_data) with _target.call{value: address(this).balance}(_data), so the sent value equals the contract's entire balance instead of the _value argument.
Replace onlyOwner modifier body with an empty body, removing the owner check so anyone can call sendMoney.
